Where each delivery goes

Every reference on the schedule, located from the master plan. Each one comes from the tag printed on the unit or from the callout's leader line, followed to its arrow. Each has a GPS point and the nearest sector, gate, street and park. These are drawing positions, not measured on site. Check on arrival and pin it on the dashboard.

How this was read

The master plan is a vector drawing, so every word on it can be read with its exact position. That's 4,049 labels. Each unit's small tag (for example "P38") sits on the unit itself.

The buildings, toilets and generators sheets use large numbered bubbles with a leader line to the unit. Each leader was followed to its arrow tip. Where both exist they agree: P06, WC01, AA and HRP land within about 3 m of each other.

Sheet positions are converted to GPS with the satellite alignment already used by the plan explorer. That alignment is about ±0.7 m, and the drawing itself is not a survey.

"Area only" means the line names a place the master labels, such as Helen Park, sector S18 or Turn 2, but not a spot.

"Not found" means no tag, callout or place word exists for it on any of the eight drawings. Those need a location from the branch or the crew.
